statement: Test encrypted_manifest_keeps_versioned_metadata_private: symlink name, symlink target, and macOS flags metadata under POSIX and platform-security features are absent from ciphertext and restored exactly after unlock.
FEATURE_PRIVATE_RESOURCE_DECLARATION_V1 is forbidden on unencrypted archives: setting it and encoding natively fails with UnsupportedRequiredFeature.

Test multiple_hybrid_recipients: two X-Wing recipients with different label lengths both unlock; a non-recipient identity gets CryptoNoMatchingRecipient; duplicate recipients are refused with CryptoRecipientPolicyInvalid.

Test password_archive_unlocks: the correct password opens; a wrong password returns CryptoNoMatchingRecipient, the same code as a non-matching identity. The destination-absence assertion is vacuous because open_encrypted writes nothing.

Test embedded_signature_and_recipient_mutation: after embedding a signature and adding a recipient, content and physical bindings stay Valid and addressing becomes Stale; reencrypt_recipients removes the first identity while preserving LAI and AUX.
Test password_change_rotates_the_key: change_password makes the old password fail with CryptoNoMatchingRecipient, the new one opens, LAI and AUX are unchanged, and PCI changes.

Test encrypted_filesystem_pack: default encrypted pack uses planner balanced-enc-v1 and chunker gear-norm-secret-table-v1/..., two packs share LAI/AUX but differ in PCI; BoundaryMode::PhteAes128 with Fast gives fast-enc-v1 and phte-aes128-norm-v1/....
research_needed: Measure CDC boundary/size leakage of secret-gear-table vs PHTE-AES128 modes against chosen-plaintext fingerprinting.

statement: Test every_padding_mode_round_trips: PaddingMode None, Bucketed, Maximum each encrypt, record the mode publicly, and reopen; no size or leakage property is asserted.
research_needed: Empirically measure length leakage and overhead per padding schedule on realistic archive-size distributions.

statement: Test commitment_envelope_ciphertext_footer_and_truncation: tampered commitment gives CryptoKeyCommitmentFailed, envelope MAC gives CryptoEnvelopeAuthFailed, ciphertext gives CryptoAeadAuthFailed; truncation by 1/191/193 gives TruncatedFooter or IncorrectTotalLength. Encrypted footer is 192 bytes.
The encrypted footer tamper case asserts only is_err(), and truncation accepts either of two codes, although project rules require each negative case to assert a stable reason code.
refines_or_supersedes: CONTRIBUTING.md:182-183 (each negative case must assert a stable reason code)
decision_needed: Which exact reason code must a footer-byte mutation in an encrypted archive produce?

statement: Test recipient_and_segment_reordering: reordered or duplicated stanzas give CryptoRecipientStanzaInvalid; unknown stanza type or malformed encapsulation give CryptoNoMatchingRecipient; segment reorder or locator mutation give CryptoSegmentStructureInvalid; splicing gives CryptoAeadAuthFailed; max_segments=1 gives CryptoResourcePolicyRefused.

Test unknown_required_crypto_feature_fails_before_recipient_work: setting incompat feature bit 63 on an encrypted archive yields CryptoSuiteUnsupported; the test checks the code, not that recipient work was skipped.
research_needed: Instrument or time the open path to prove unknown features are rejected before KEM/KDF work.

statement: Crypto test helpers assume layout: envelope section at offset 256 with 64-byte header and 16-byte record prefix; stanza sequence is envelope field 8; footer is 192 bytes with segments-section offset at footer+40..48 and segments digest at footer+104..136.

No integration test covers RFC 3161 timestamp verification, detached signature verification through the library, encrypted STREAM (refused), or remote key management; timestamps are tested only in the crypto/timestamp.rs unit module (1 test).
evidence_in_source: integration test list; unit test counts via grep (crypto/timestamp.rs has 1 #[test])
research_needed: Interop tests with real TSA tokens (e.g. freetsa, DigiCert) and certificate-path edge cases.

statement: Test filesystem_round_trip: packing a generated tree is byte-deterministic, preserves empty directories, file bytes, and file mtime; multi-chunk file splits under the chunker gear-norm-v1/min-131072/target-524288/max-2097152; executable bit asserted only on unix.

Test filesystem_creation_order_cannot_change_cdc_output: reversing file creation order keeps LAI and PCR equal; container bytes may differ because Windows creation order/time is captured as AUX metadata.
evidence_in_source: integration test assertion and inline comment L136-137
decision_needed: Should default packing capture Windows creation time, given it makes containers differ for identical logical trees?

statement: Test extraction_refuses_file_and_directory_collisions: existing file, file-where-directory-expected, and directory-where-file-expected each fail with ExtractionCollision and leave the pre-existing object untouched.

Test corruption_and_policy_refusal_happen_before_materialization: section digest corruption (SectionDigestMismatch) and entry_count=0 policy (PolicyRefused/ResourceLimit) create no destination; understated preamble budget (bytes 96..104) gives Corrupt/ResourceLimit.
Test invalid_logical_path_is_rejected_before_destination_creation: rewriting a manifest path component to '.' yields DotComponent without creating the destination.

Test partial_failure_never_overwrites_preexisting_files: when a collision occurs at 'zz', the earlier entry 'a' has already been written and remains; INDEXED extraction is not transactional, only non-overwriting.
decision_needed: Should INDEXED unpack preflight collisions or stage output so failures leave no partial tree (as STREAM unpack does)?

statement: Test pack_captures_symlinks_without_following_them (cfg(unix) only): a dangling relative symlink is captured as a Symlink entry with exact target bytes.

Integration tests have no Windows-specific coverage (junctions, symlinks, ADS, ACL or security-descriptor restore); platform branches are cfg(unix) only, leaving Windows metadata to src unit tests and record vectors.
evidence_in_source: cfg(unix) at L84, L259, L297; no cfg(windows) in tests
research_needed: Windows integration tests for reparse points, ADS, security descriptors, case-insensitive collisions, long paths.

statement: Test selected_multi_chunk_jpeg_region: planner dense-v6 on a 1024x1024 quality-96 tiled JPEG split into 64 KiB chunks selects exactly one multi-chunk jpeg-jxl reconstruction region with worst reconstructed bytes equal to region logical bytes.

Region negative cases with conformance ids: clearing the feature gives UnsupportedRequiredFeature; ECF-REGION-MISSING-001 UnknownReconstructionRegion; -ACCESS-001 InvalidRegionAccess; -RANGE-001 InvalidReconstructionRegion; -OVERLAP-001 OverlappingReconstructionRegion; -WRITER-REVERIFY-001 MalformedReconstructionPayload.

JPEG region encoding is deterministic and identity-neutral versus v5 planning (LAI, AUX, PCR equal; PCI differs); caller limits of 8 MiB window / 128 MiB working set are refused with ResourceLimit; restored bytes equal the original.
research_needed: Measure real peak memory of JXL reconstruction versus declared requirement.

statement: Test whole_object_jpeg_regions_survive_the_sequential_layout: regions round-trip through STREAM with reconstruction_integrity set and chunks equal to INDEXED; flipping a middle byte makes sequential open fail (no specific code asserted).

Test balanced_retains_independent_access_and_small_jpeg_falls_back: default Balanced packing of a 32x32 JPEG creates no region, records audits and a fallback reason, and keeps every chunk independently decodable.

Test a_chunk_shared_by_distinct_content_objects_makes_regions_ineligible: when a JPEG chunk is also referenced by another ContentObject, dense-v6 selects no region and records audit reason RegionDedupConflict.
research_needed: Frequency of dedup conflicts on real photo libraries with duplicates/edits.

statement: Test helper recomputes region identity as SHA-256 over domain 'entrybound/reconstruction-region/jpeg-jxl/v1\0', content object, start index, chunk count, plan ref, byte counts, access fields, and representation digest.

JPEG reconstruction tests use only synthetic baseline RGB JPEGs from the image crate (noise and tiled patterns); no progressive, EXIF/ICC, CMYK, restart-marker, arithmetic-coded, truncated, or camera-produced JPEGs are exercised.
research_needed: Run reconstruction success rate, savings, and time on a representative real JPEG corpus (cameras, phones, web, scanned).

statement: Test empty_archive_round_trips: an archive with no entries encodes, opens to an equal Archive, and verify returns the same report as open.

FEATURE_POSIX_METADATA_V1 must be set exactly when POSIX Entry v2 semantics (symlink, uid, gid) are present, in INDEXED and STREAM; missing the bit or setting it without such semantics fails with UnsupportedRequiredFeature.
All members of a hardlink group must agree on inode-scoped metadata; members differing in uid make encode fail with InvalidHardlinkGroup.
Test complete_in_memory_fixture: encoding is deterministic; open reports index PresentValid, canonical_encoding, chunk_integrity, pci_computed; six file entries dedupe to five content objects.
Test logical_and_auxiliary_identity_change_for_the_right_reasons: changing mtime alters AUX but not LAI; changing the executable bit or file content alters LAI.
Test rechunking_preserves_logical_identity_and_changes_pcr: 1 MiB versus 512 KiB fixed chunking keeps LAI and AUX while PCR differs.

The Index is optional and never changes semantics: an absent Index is reported RebuiltAbsent/IndexAbsentRebuilt, a misleading offset RebuiltInvalid/IndexInvalidRebuilt, with identical LAI/PCR/AUX and entries; only PCI differs.

Test generated_native_conformance_corpus mutates one valid archive into 15 cases ECF-F001..F015 (bad magic, unsupported version, unknown required feature, total length, record length, field order, duplicate/unknown field, section/chunk digest, LAI/PCR/AUX, entry identity/aux) plus truncation and invalid index.

Conformance mappings: F001 BadMagic, F002 UnsupportedVersion, F003 UnsupportedRequiredFeature, F004 IncorrectTotalLength, F005 SectionStructure, F006 NoncanonicalEncoding, F007 DuplicateSemanticDeclaration, F008 NoncanonicalEncoding, F009 SectionDigestMismatch, F010 ChunkDigestMismatch, F011-F013 Lai/Pcr/AuxMismatch, F014 EntryIdentityMismatch, F015 EntryAuxMismatch.

Wire offsets asserted by the corpus: format version at bytes 8..10 (major 1 is UnsupportedVersion), incompat features at 16..24 with a SHA-256 checksum over 16..40 stored at 40..72, and the preamble digest at footer+64..96.
Every section header begins with ASCII magic EBS1; the corpus helper asserts this for each section between preamble and footer.
Test diagnostic_classes_remain_distinguishable: unsupported major version maps to OutcomeClass::Unsupported and one-byte truncation to OutcomeClass::Truncated.

The native conformance corpus exists only as in-memory mutations inside a Rust test; there is no exported corpus with expected outcomes that an independent or minimal reader in another language could consume.
research_needed: Build an exporter emitting case bytes plus expected class/code manifest; run a second implementation against it.
decision_needed: Will v1 publish a language-neutral conformance corpus and observed-outcome manifest?

statement: Native fixtures declare format namespace ecf/bootstrap-v1, format_major 0 / format_minor 1, identity profile IdentityV1, digest algorithm SHA-256, layout Indexed, role Complete.
decision_needed: When does the format leave major version 0 / ecf/bootstrap-v1 and what compatibility promise applies then?

statement: Random-access tests use a loopback plain-HTTP/1.1 server that answers HEAD with Content-Length, Accept-Ranges, strong ETag, and serves single-range 206 responses, asserting the client sends If-Match with the ETag and Accept-Encoding identity.
research_needed: No HTTPS, HTTP/2, CDN (S3/CloudFront/GitHub releases) behaviour, multi-range, 200-for-range, or ETag change mid-session in integration tests.

statement: Test http_indexed_read_fetches_only_metadata_and_requested_closure: reading one small entry fetches less than half the archive, bytes_fetched equals server-transferred bytes, and whole_archive_verified stays false.
research_needed: Measure request count and latency versus archive size and RTT; the only threshold asserted is less than 50% of bytes.

statement: Test http_encrypted_indexed_read_authenticates_without_full_download: public encrypted inspection and identity-unlocked entry reads over HTTP fetch fewer bytes than the full container and are not whole-archive verified.

Test http_password_indexed_read_keeps_kdf_and_decryption_client_side: password-protected remote reads succeed with partial fetch; the test does not instrument the server to prove no secret leaves the client.

Test random_access_fetches_dictionary_and_bounded_lookback_dependencies: in-memory random reads of dictionary-backed (Balanced) and lookback-grouped (Dense) entries return exact bytes with dictionaries_verified, groups_verified, and dependency_chunk_count above 0.
Test random_access_verifies_deflate_reconstruction_dependencies: a Dense-planned gzip file with reconstruction data is read randomly with exact original bytes and reconstruction_verified true.

Test v5_selected_reconstruction_round_trips: planner v5 Dense on a flate2 level-6 gzip fixture selects deflate-reconstruct/v1, encodes deterministically, verifies reconstruction_integrity, and keeps LAI/AUX/PCR equal to v4 planning.
Test deflate_reconstruction_survives_the_sequential_layout: reconstruction data round-trips through STREAM with equal identities (except PCI) and reconstruction_integrity true.

Test missing_corrupt_or_undeclared_reconstruction_fails_typed: missing data gives UnknownReconstructionData, a flipped data byte gives ReconstructionDataDigestMismatch, and a cleared FEATURE_RECONSTRUCTIVE_TRANSFORM_V1 gives UnsupportedRequiredFeature.

Reconstruction fallback reasons are canonical and explainable: non-DEFLATE input records UnrecognizedOrVerificationFailed, and explain renders 'unrecognized-or-verification-failed=1, complete-cost-rejected=0'.
evidence_in_source: integration test assertion of exact string

statement: DEFLATE reconstruction is tested only on gzip produced by flate2 at level 6 on synthetic CSV-like text; other producers (zlib levels, libdeflate, zopfli, 7-Zip, pigz, Java, .NET) are not exercised.
research_needed: Measure preflate reconstruction success rate, reconstruction-data size, and CPU time across real DEFLATE producers and ZIP/PNG/docx corpora.

statement: The STREAM writer must work with a sink implementing only Write (never seeks) and the reader with a source implementing only Read that returns small partial reads; the tests enforce this by type.

For all four profiles, INDEXED and STREAM layouts of the same archive have identical LAI, AUX, PCR, entries, objects, chunks, dictionaries, groups, reconstruction data/regions, plans, and fidelity; only PCI and physical order may differ.
Inspecting a STREAM archive reports layout Stream, index NotApplicableStream, index not applicable, random_entry_lookup false, stream feature present, and the declared dedup window.

Tests shared_dictionaries_survive_the_sequential_layout and bounded_lookback_groups_survive_the_sequential_layout: dictionaries and ChunkGroups round-trip through STREAM (64-byte and 1-byte drip reads) and unpack exactly.

Default StreamWriteOptions uses dedup window 0; a plan referencing an earlier object's chunk fails with StreamWindowExceeded/PolicyRefused naming the needed window; StreamWindow::Ceiling at the requirement succeeds, one below fails; Auto declares the exact minimum.
research_needed: Measure how often real trees need a nonzero window and the reader memory cost of large windows.

statement: A STREAM reader rejects a body whose references exceed the preamble-declared dedup window (bytes 160..168) with StreamWindowExceeded classified Nonconforming.
STREAM truncation at any cut point (0, inside preamble, body, or footer) is reported as Truncated/TruncatedStream, while trailing bytes after a complete footer are Corrupt/IncorrectTotalLength.
Unknown STREAM item tags are refused, never skipped (tag 0xfff0 gives Unsupported/UnsupportedRequiredFeature); a bytes pattern that is neither item header nor footer gives StreamItemOrdering.
decision_needed: Is there any skippable/optional STREAM item class for forward compatibility, or are all unknown tags fatal forever?

statement: STREAM ordering rules: a manifest record appearing before the chunk data it describes gives StreamForwardReference (Nonconforming); a duplicated TransformPlans item gives DuplicateSemanticDeclaration.
Corrupting a STREAM chunk frame payload gives OutcomeClass::Corrupt (no code asserted); corrupting the Dictionaries item gives SectionDigestMismatch/Corrupt.
Caller policy stops a sequential pass early: max_container_bytes at half the stream, or a chunk_count budget of 1, gives PolicyRefused/ResourceLimit.

An undeclared STREAM budget writes a default ResourceBudget, reports budget_declared false, still carries actual entry and chunk totals in the footer, and is never treated as unlimited: caller limits still refuse.

Test staging_spills_within_its_memory_bound: with 8 KiB staging memory and a 64 MiB total, unpack_stream spills to temp files named entrybound-stage-<pid>-*, keeps peak resident staging at most 8 KiB + 96 KiB, and cleans up after success and truncation failure.
research_needed: Validate staging bounds and temp-disk usage on multi-GB archives and low-disk conditions; fixtures here are under 1 MiB.

statement: STREAM extraction never materializes unverified content: corrupting the final chunk frame creates no destination at all, and existing destination files are never replaced (ExtractionCollision).
research_needed: Cost of whole-stream staging before any output for very large archives (disk and time); streaming-to-pipe use cases.
decision_needed: Is an opt-in progressive (unverified-until-end) extraction mode ever allowed?

statement: Layout discrimination: INDEXED preamble byte 72 = 1 with bytes 160..176 zero and no STREAM feature; STREAM byte 72 = 2 with FEATURE_STREAM_LAYOUT_V1. Each reader refuses the other layout with UnsupportedRequiredFeature.

Test the_writer_is_deterministic_and_verification_is_repeatable: identical STREAM bytes on two writes; body length equals total minus 256-byte preamble and STREAM footer; verify_stream reports canonical, chunk, content, LAI/PCR/AUX integrity and PCI.

STREAM framing per the test walker: each item starts with STREAM_ITEM_MAGIC and u16 tag; chunk frames carry a 64- or 96-byte frame header (96 when incompat bit 0x1 is set) then stored bytes; other items carry an 8-byte length and 32 further bytes plus payload.

STREAM tests use generated trees of at most a few hundred KiB per file; no test exercises archives larger than RAM, millions of entries, or long-running pipes, so scalability guarantees rest on design.
evidence_in_source: fixture sizes in write_rich_source and write_similar_source
research_needed: Scale tests: >RAM archives, 10^6-10^7 entries, sustained pipe throughput, peak memory profiling.

statement: CLI test all_native_commands_operate_on_real_archives covers ebound pack, verify ('exact-byte PCI'), list (tab-separated kind and path), inspect (format ecf/bootstrap-v1, planner balanced-v6, gear-norm-v1 chunker, codec usage, index state), explain, and unpack.
--profile is accepted only at pack time ('pack --profile dense' gives planner dense-v6); passing --profile to verify fails with usage diagnostic EB_CLI_USAGE.
Malformed input must print a stable class and reason code ('NONCONFORMING EB_ECF_BAD_MAGIC') on stderr, exit nonzero, and never print Rust Debug structures.

CLI STREAM over pipes: 'pack <dir> - --layout stream' writes archive bytes to stdout with all status on stderr; verify, list, inspect, explain, and unpack accept '-' stdin; stored bytes begin with magic 8E 45 42 31 0D 0A 1A 0A and byte 72 = 2.
A STREAM archive stored in a seekable file must never be reported as random access: inspect says random entry lookup unavailable, and list warns on stderr that it required a complete sequential pass.
A truncated STREAM read from stdin exits with process exit code 3 (TRUNCATED class) and prints 'TRUNCATED EB_ECF_TRUNCATED_STREAM'.
decision_needed: Is the full outcome-class-to-exit-code mapping documented and frozen for v1?

statement: CLI STREAM pack with default window refuses a tree whose files share a chunk (EB_ECF_STREAM_WINDOW_EXCEEDED, mentions automatic window) and leaves no output file; '--stream-window auto' succeeds with a nonzero window and verifies.
decision_needed: Should the CLI default for STREAM be auto rather than 0, given ordinary duplicate files trigger refusal?

statement: CLI crypto test: pack --recipient (.ebk key files); inspect --crypto shows 'private archive metadata: locked' without names; verify without identity prints 'PRIVATE CONTENT UNVERIFIED'; verify/unpack --identity authenticate; inspect with identity shows Descriptor version 2.

CLI crypto test continued: tampered ciphertext unpack fails with no destination; key generate-signing; sign --embed; verify --signatures --require-addressing-signature; key add makes addressing STALE; key list shows 2 fingerprints; key remove --retain revokes the old identity.

CLI test detached_signing_cli_enforces_requested_bindings: sign --detached writes a .ebsig file for an unencrypted archive, and verify --signature with --require-content-signature and --require-physical-signature succeeds.
The CLI 'salvage' command is recognised but unimplemented: running 'ebound salvage' returns ReasonCode::CommandNotImplemented (EB_CLI_NOT_IMPLEMENTED).
research_needed: Define salvage semantics (corruption localization, partial recovery) and evaluate on damaged-archive corpora.
decision_needed: Is salvage in or out of v1 scope?

statement: Encrypted STREAM creation is unsupported: 'pack ... - --layout stream --recipient ...' fails with CryptoLayoutUnsupported before any input or output is touched.
refines_or_supersedes: CONTRIBUTING.md:179-180 (encrypted STREAM must fail before output)
decision_needed: Will encrypted STREAM layout exist in v1 or remain refused?

statement: Password and hybrid-recipient protection cannot be combined in one CLI pack invocation: --recipient with --password fails with CryptoRecipientPolicyInvalid.
decision_needed: Is mixing password and X-Wing recipients forbidden by format or only by CLI policy?

statement: CLI usage validation: --stream-window with --layout indexed and an unknown --layout value (e.g. 'mounted') both fail with CommandUsage.

No integration test in crates/entrybound/tests covers legacy import, compatibility or preservation modes, export, sidecars, or migration; legacy behaviour is tested only by src unit modules (zip 13, sevenz 11, export 13, tar 6, stream 5, import 3, lom 1, migration 1) and CLI unit tests.

research_needed: End-to-end legacy round-trip tests against real-world archives from many producers.

research_needed: Benchmark corpus (Silesia, source trees, VM images, photos, logs) comparing profiles with zstd/xz/7z/zpaq/borg/restic.

statement: Integration test suite totals 78 #[test] functions across 11 files (stream_layout 18, crypto_v1 12, native_ecf 9, filesystem_workflow 7, compression_planner 6, cdc_dedup 5, crypto_primitives 5, random_access 5, jpeg 4, reconstructive 4, cross_file 3); CLI integration adds 11.

statement: The crypto vector helper is a separate non-production package (publish=false, own empty workspace) depending on aes-gcm-siv =0.12.1, argon2 =0.6.0, hkdf =0.13.0, sha2 =0.11.0; its fixed inputs are unsafe for real encryption.
The Rust vector generator uses the same crates and versions as production, so its vectors are not independent of production primitives; independence rests on reference.py.
research_needed: Confirm vectors against at least one non-RustCrypto implementation for every primitive and derivation.

statement: README: two non-production generators for docs/crypto-wire-v1.md vectors (Rust with pinned RustCrypto; independent Python building T1, ECF records, private-object envelopes, sequences). Both print identical key=value lines; --canonical-only needs only the Python stdlib.
Python reference environment pins argon2-cffi 25.1.0, argon2-cffi-bindings 26.1.0, cffi 2.1.1, cryptography 46.0.3, pycparser 3.0.

Vector helper constants: format namespace ecf/bootstrap-v1 and X-Wing parameters xwing-mlkem768-x25519-sha3-256/draft-10; T1 encoding is u16 label length, label, u16 field count, then per field u16 tag (1-based), u64 length, value.

Recipient wrap-key derivation: method context is T1 'entrybound/recipient-method-context/v1' over stanza version, type, class, id, 16-byte zero hint, parameters, encapsulation; HKDF-Extract(salt=archive id, method secret) then Expand T1 'entrybound/recipient-wrap-key/v1' to 32 bytes.

Wrap associated data is T1 'entrybound/recipient-wrap-ad/v1' over namespace, format 0.1, crypto version 1, suite 1, archive id, stanza fields, parameters, encapsulation, and nonce; the 32-byte AFK is wrapped with AES-256-GCM-SIV.

The password-recipient vector uses Argon2id parameters encoded as 'A2ID' version 19, memory 262144 KiB (256 MiB), 3 passes, parallelism 4, 16-byte salt; no memory/latency measurement is cited for this cost on low-end or mobile devices.
research_needed: Measure unlock time and memory on low-end laptops, phones, and WASM; compare with OWASP/RFC 9106 recommendations.
decision_needed: Are 256 MiB / t=3 / p=4 the production defaults, and is a lower-memory profile permitted?

statement: Container vectors: recipient directory entry is record type 22 version 1 with fields id (type 7), stanza type (type 2), fingerprint (type 7), label (type 8); EBCS sequence is magic, version 1, kind, reserved u32, u64 count, length-prefixed items; EBPO object is magic, version 1, kind, reserved u32, payload.

The helper emits only vector groups V5 (hybrid stanza wrap), V6 (password KDF and wrap), and S1-S7 (empty, one, multi, private control object, plus invalid out-of-order, duplicate, truncated sequences).

Neither generator produces V1 (root hierarchy and commitment), V2 (segment nonces/AD), V3 (envelope canonicalization), V4 (X-Wing combiner), V7 (signature transcripts), or V8 vectors; V5 uses a synthetic 1120-byte pattern instead of a real X-Wing encapsulation.
evidence_in_source: generator code; docs/crypto-wire-v1-vectors.txt contains only V5, V6, S1-S7 keys (42 lines)
research_needed: Independent (non-Rust) regeneration of V1-V4, V7, V8 including real X-Wing, HMAC commitment, segment derivation, Ed25519 transcripts, and PHTE/secret-gear boundary derivations.

statement: Helper self-test corrected_wrap_and_sequence_vectors_are_stable pins V5 and V6 wrap-AD SHA-256, wrapped-AFK ciphertexts, and the S1 empty-sequence hash; the name reflects a prior correction of published V5 values.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/crypto-wire-v1.md:944 mentions the previous V5 wrap-AD hash

statement: The Python reference independently implements T1 encoding and HKDF-SHA-256 (extract and expand) using only the hashlib and hmac standard libraries.

In --canonical-only mode reference.py substitutes a hard-coded Argon2id output instead of recomputing it, so that mode does not independently check V6_ARGON2ID_OUTPUT or the two wrapped-AFK ciphertexts.
research_needed: Ensure full mode (argon2-cffi + cryptography) is run and recorded for each vector revision.

statement: Full mode computes the V5/V6 wrapped AFKs with pyca cryptography's AESGCMSIV (OpenSSL-backed), an implementation independent of RustCrypto aes-gcm-siv.

ZIP compatibility probes are development tooling only and never run by production; the checked matrix is behavioural evidence, and changing a frozen profile requires a new versioned profile ID and a reviewed matrix update.
Matrix regeneration refuses to run unless runtimes match exactly: CPython 3.13.5, OpenJDK/Temurin 21.0.12.1, and bsdtar/libarchive 3.8.8.
Regeneration writes the corpus to target/zip-compat-corpus, compiles ZipProbe.java into target/zip-compat-probe, and rewrites tools/zip-compat/observed-outcomes-v1.json.

Matrix schema zip-observed-outcomes/v1 records host platform, four runtime profile ids with version strings, and per case the source SHA-256 plus python_zipfile, java_zipfile, java_zipinputstream, libarchive_bsdtar observations.
The libarchive probe shells out to the system 'tar' (-tf listing, -xOf per name to stdout) with a hard-coded runtime label; it relies on the host tar being bsdtar.

The adversarial ZIP corpus has 14 generated cases: ordinary-store, ordinary-deflate, local/central name, method, CRC and size disagreements, descriptor-crc, duplicate-name, unsafe-parent, unicode-conflict, directory-type, and deflate-trailing.

Every corpus case is a single-entry (or two-entry duplicate) ZIP with version 20, zero timestamps, and no comment; ZIP64, encryption, data descriptors without signature, prepended data, multi-disk, symlink attributes, NTFS/Unix extra timestamps, and CP437 names are not probed.
research_needed: Extend differential corpus to ZIP64, AES/ZipCrypto flags, prepended/SFX data, extra-field conflicts, symlinks, and real producer archives.

statement: The Python probe lists infolist() names, reads each unique name via getinfo (last duplicate wins), records length and SHA-256 or the exception class, and emits compact sorted JSON with runtime label zip/python-zipfile@<version>.

The Java probe runs java.util.zip.ZipFile (central-directory lookup via getEntry) and ZipInputStream (sequential scan, last same-name entry retained, stream error recorded); both hard-code runtime label 21.0.12.1.
All ZIP probes read member bytes into memory or stdout; none extracts to a filesystem, so traversal, directory, permission, symlink, and overwrite behaviour of the reference runtimes is not observed.
research_needed: Add sandboxed extraction probes (zipfile.extractall, unzip, bsdtar -x, Explorer, macOS Archive Utility) recording created files.

statement: Matrix v1 was observed only on Windows-11-10.0.26200 with CPython 3.13.5 (MSC, AMD64), OpenJDK 21.0.12.1 LTS, and the Windows-bundled bsdtar 3.8.8 (zlib 1.2.13.1-motley, liblzma 5.8.1, bz2lib 1.0.8, libzstd 1.5.7, cng 2.0).
research_needed: Repeat on Linux/macOS builds of the same runtimes; add Info-ZIP unzip, 7-Zip, Windows Explorer, macOS Archive Utility, .NET, Go archive/zip, Rust zip crate.
decision_needed: Which additional runtimes must have frozen compatibility profiles for v1 adoption?

statement: Central CRC mismatch: Python zipfile reads raise BadZipFile; Java ZipFile and ZipInputStream both return the 7 payload bytes; bsdtar fails listing ('Error exit delayed').

statement: The strict-tar differential probe is development-only: it generates inputs, asks local Python tarfile and system tar to list/read them, and prints JSON for manual comparison before intentionally updating evidence.
Tar probe corpus: six ustar cases (mode 0644, uid/gid 0, mtime 1700000000): ordinary, duplicate-name, path-traversal ../outside, single-zero-end-block, nonzero-after-end, bad-checksum.
Unlike the ZIP harness, the tar probe records but does not enforce runtime versions; system tar is only listed with 'tar -tf', not extracted, and Python extraction reads members to memory.

statement: Tar evidence schema entrybound/tar-differential-evidence/v1 was observed on Windows-11-10.0.26200 with Python tarfile 3.13.5 and bsdtar/libarchive 3.8.8.
Ordinary ustar member: Python tarfile, bsdtar, and Entrybound strict all accept.
Duplicate member name: Python tarfile and bsdtar accept and list both; Entrybound strict refuses under unique-path invariants.
Member '../outside': Python tarfile and bsdtar accept for listing; Entrybound strict refuses with EB_TAR_UNSAFE_PATH.
Archive terminated by one zero block instead of two: Python tarfile and bsdtar accept; Entrybound strict refuses with EB_TAR_STRUCTURE_INVALID.
Nonzero bytes after the end-of-archive marker: Python tarfile and bsdtar ignore them and accept; Entrybound strict refuses with EB_TAR_STRUCTURE_INVALID.
Corrupted header checksum: Python tarfile raises ReadError, bsdtar exits 1, Entrybound strict refuses with EB_TAR_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH; all three agree.

The 'entrybound-strict' column and 'accepted-listing' labels are not produced by probe.py, so the evidence file was curated by hand; its duplicate-name reason EB_DUPLICATE_LOGICAL_PATH does not match the code string EB_EAM_DUPLICATE_LOGICAL_PATH.
